name: Week 24 KB Tuesday — Two Flows Back From the Bench 🌀 (B-Stance Flow + Leggy Flow)
description:
After the fourteen-move gauntlet, this Tuesday goes the other way: two flows you already know, run for quality instead of learning.

The **B-Stance Flow** comes back after a long absence — five moves built on the offset stance, where one leg takes most of the load and the other just keeps you honest. Then the **Leggy Flow**, the lower-body chain, with no overhead work in it at all.

**Warmup reminder:** around-the-body passes → halo → bottoms-up press (18lb) → cossack squats → internal core fist rotation → protective behind-back shrug, then the 7-move banded prep.

Strict press and KB row run between the two flows. Cossacks come back into the warmup after a long time away.

dayOverview.theme: Two known flows instead of one new one — the B-Stance Flow returns after its longest absence in the program, paired with the Leggy Flow. Both are single-bell chains you can run for quality rather than order. Cossack squats come back into the warmup. Strength (strict press + row) runs between the flows so nothing stacks at the top. Almost no overhead volume today, which is a deliberate break after the gauntlet week.

spotlights.why: The B-stance is the whole reason this flow is worth bringing back, and it's the beat most likely to get sloppy through neglect. The back foot is a kickstand, not a second leg — it's there for balance and takes almost none of the load, which means the front hip has to do a job it never has to do in a normal two-legged swing. Done right it's most of a single-leg hinge without the balance tax. The spotlight is keeping the weight honestly on the front leg: if you can feel the back foot pushing, the load has quietly redistributed and the whole point is gone.

You said it yourself last time these showed up — they used to feel impossible and need support, and now they don't. That's a genuine floor rise, and the reason to spotlight them isn't to load them but to bank the range while the pattern is honest. Depth is the project now: sit into one hip with the heel down, the other leg straight, and get lower than feels comfortable without letting the down heel lift. They also work as an early-warning system — how they feel in the warmup tells you what the legs have got before the session commits to anything.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Tuesday content rotates: W21 GymFiesta circuit + Dead Cluster Flow · W23 Long Coordination Gauntlet + figure-8 switch-clean · W24 B-Stance Flow + Leggy Flow, cossacks back in the warmup (current) · W25 candidates — the Dead Cluster Flow, the overhead mobility complex, or the gauntlet's return now the order's known. Every week pulls at least one thing off the bench.
watchpoints: **🌀🔆 B-Stance Flow (@Asgooch) — back after its longest absence.** b-stance swing → swing clean → ab-stance goblet squat → swing snatch → overhead lunge. One continuous chain per side. (Canonical: kb-b-stance-flow.)
**🔆 The B-stance is the point: the back foot is a KICKSTAND** 🛑. Balance only — the front leg takes the load. If you feel the back foot pushing, reset the stance.

**🌀 Leggy Flow — the lower-body chain, no overhead.** dead clean → curtsy lunge → lateral lunge → lateral squat clean → lateral lunge → tactical clean. Medium bell, quality over load. (Canonical: kb-leggy-flow.)
**🔆 Cossacks are back in the warmup** — depth is the project now that they run unassisted. Heel down, sit low, both sides.
**Light on overhead today, on purpose** — one snatch and one lunge in the B-stance flow and nothing else. The gauntlet week was overhead-heavy; this is the counterweight.
**Strict overhead press holds 50 at 8/8/8** 🛑 — strict, no push-press, both sides even. KB row at 40.
**Strength runs BETWEEN the two flows** so the demanding volume isn't stacked at the top.
**Leg-athletic on Tuesday is free** — both flows are lunge-heavy and Friday is three days out.
**Protective behind-back shrug greasing set stays in the warm-up.**

sets.name: 🔆 Warm-Up — Around-the-Body Passes + Cossacks + Cuff Prep

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 25lb, light and fun. Bell passes hand to hand around the waist, hips still.
- **Stay tall, no leaning** — the bell orbits you, you don't orbit it
- Hand-eye primer; both directions
**LOAD:** 15-20lb. Big slow circles both directions — open the shoulders.
**LOAD:** 18lb. Inverted bell over a vertical forearm, grip hard, shoulder packed. Cuff prep.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT (warmup slot) — bodyweight, slow. Back in the rotation after a long absence.**
- **Sit into one hip, other leg straight, DOWN heel stays planted** — if the heel lifts, you've gone past your range
- **Chest up** through the bottom, don't fold forward to fake depth
- **Depth is the project** — these run unassisted now, so the range is what's left to build. Go lower than comfortable and hold a beat
- Take note of how they feel: it's the earliest read you get on what the legs have today
Standing, hinged slightly forward. Tight fists, thumbs tucked — grip + forearm primer.

exercises.equipment: light DB pair or a KB held behind the body
exercises.notes: **Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set held behind the body, palms back. Pack DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s squeeze, slow down.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~3 min)

exercises.notes: Mini-band OR blue rope band held in hands.
Elbows drive to the ribs, scaps depress.
Don't overarch the lower back to chase range.
Both arms in a V/Y, hold and breathe. Lower traps fire.

sets.notes: 1 round of all 7 banded moves (~3 min). Sustained tension, no rest between positions.

sets.name: 🌀🔆 B-Stance Flow (@Asgooch) — Back From the Bench
sets.notes:
**Single bell (~25-35lb), 3 rounds each side.** The offset-stance chain, back after its longest absence in the program.

**🔆 The B-stance is the whole lift** — and it's the thing that decays when a flow sits on the bench:
- **The back foot is a KICKSTAND.** Toe lightly down, heel up, balance only. It takes almost none of the load
- **The front leg does the work** — this is most of a single-leg hinge without the balance tax
- **If you can feel the back foot pushing, reset.** That's the load redistributing and the point of the flow leaking away
- **Hips drive the swing and the snatch**, arm stays a rope

**The ab-stance goblet squat** alternates wide and narrow — let the stance change be deliberate, not incidental.

🛑 **One snatch and one overhead lunge is all the overhead today** — pack the shoulder DOWN on both, ribs down on the lunge.

**Reflection:** on the b-stance swing, can you honestly say the front leg is carrying it — or has the back foot turned into a second leg? That's the difference between this flow and a regular swing.

sets.name: Strength — Strict Press + KB Row (Between the Flows) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50 across all sets — strict single-arm press, clean to rack, press straight up, NO push-press.
- **Strict, ribs DOWN**, no rib flare
- **Bicep finishes by the ear, full lockout, pack the shoulder DOWN**
- Both sides to the same standard

**LOAD:** 40. Hinged, flat back, bell to the hip.
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN and BACK** before the elbow moves — no shrugging the bell up
- **Elbow drives past the ribs**, not flared wide
- Slow return, full stretch at the bottom

sets.notes: 3 rounds, run between the two flows so the demanding volume isn't stacked at the top.

sets.name: 🌀 Leggy Flow — the Lower-Body Chain (No Overhead)
sets.notes:
**Single MEDIUM bell (~25-35lb), 3 rounds each side.** The lower-body chain — dead clean → curtsy lunge → lateral lunge → lateral squat clean → lateral lunge → tactical clean, all on one side before switching.

**Nothing goes overhead here**, which is why it closes a day that already ran a snatch and an overhead lunge. The shoulder gets the back half of the session off.

- **The cleans come from the LEGS and hips**, not the arm — the arm is a hook
- **Curtsy and lateral lunges: knee tracks the toes**, chest up, don't collapse inward
- **Let each move feed the next** — the chain shouldn't have stops in it

**Reflection:** the two lateral lunges bracket the lateral squat clean — does that middle section flow as one movement now, or are you resetting between them?

exercises.notes: 60s each side. Hip flexor release — counters the lunges and the b-stance work.
60s. Adductors + inner hips — the cossacks and lateral lunges bill here.

tips: **B-Stance Flow is back** — b-stance swing → swing clean → ab-stance goblet squat → swing snatch → overhead lunge, one chain per side.
🔆 **The back foot is a kickstand, not a second leg.** If it's pushing, reset the stance.
**Leggy Flow closes the day** — six moves, no overhead, medium bell, quality over load.
🔆 **Cossacks are back in the warmup** — unassisted now, so depth is the project. Heel down.
**Strict overhead press holds 50 at 8/8/8**; KB row at 40.
**Strength runs between the two flows** so nothing stacks at the top.
**Light on overhead today on purpose** — the counterweight to gauntlet week.
**Protective behind-back shrug greasing set in the warm-up.**
formPhilosophy: Last Tuesday asked you to hold fourteen moves in your head at once. This one asks for the opposite: two chains you already know, where nothing is new and the only thing left to work on is how well you do them. That's not a lighter week, it's a different kind of hard — a flow you half-remember will run fine and quietly teach your body the sloppy version, which is exactly what happens when something sits on the bench for a dozen weeks. The B-stance is the clearest case. Nobody misses the reps; they just stop being b-stance reps, and the back foot creeps in to help until it's a regular swing with a funny setup. Bringing a movement back is only worth it if you bring back the standard too. Building decades, not weeks.
